quests.instruction: Read the word and find the matching number!
quests.question: Eight Hundred Fifty-Two
quests.hint: Sound the word out slowly, then count that many fingers to check.
quests.explanation: "Eight Hundred Fifty-Two" is how we say the number 852 in English, so 852 is the digit that matches!
quests.funFact: If you add 0 to 852, it stays exactly the same: 852!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 0, 50, 100, 150, __?
quests.hint: The pattern counts up by 50 each time. What comes after 150?
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 50, so after 150 comes 150 + 50 = 200!
quests.funFact: The number 200 is an even number!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 753 or 404?
quests.question: 753 or 404
quests.hint: Picture counting all the way up -- whichever number you'd reach later is the answer.
quests.explanation: 753 is greater than 404 -- when counting up, 753 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you count up by ones, 753 comes right after 752!

quests.instruction: There are 82 groups of ten and 1 more. How many in total?
quests.question: 82 groups of ten and 1 more
quests.hint: Say the group total out loud, then keep counting for the leftover ones.
quests.explanation: 82 groups of ten make 820, plus 1 more makes 821!
quests.funFact: If you count backwards, 821 comes just before 822!

quests.instruction: Read the word and find the matching number!
quests.question: Five Hundred Six
quests.hint: Sound the word out slowly, then count that many fingers to check.
quests.explanation: "Five Hundred Six" is how we say the number 506 in English, so 506 is the digit that matches!
quests.funFact: Double 506 is 1012! Because 506 + 506 = 1012.

quests.instruction: What digit is in the ones place of 960?
quests.hint: Cover up every digit except the ones digit in 960.
quests.explanation: In 960, the digit 0 sits in the ones place!
quests.funFact: If you add 0 to any number, that number stays exactly the same!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 453 or 701?
quests.question: 453 or 701
quests.hint: Compare the digits from left to right: which number has more value?
quests.explanation: 701 is greater than 453 -- when counting up, 701 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you had 701 apples and found one more, you would have 702 apples!

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 505, 844, or 553?
quests.hint: Line all three numbers up in counting order first.
quests.explanation: Out of 505, 844, and 553, the number 844 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 844 by 10, it becomes 8440!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Read the numeral 956 out loud -- what word do you say?
quests.explanation: The numeral 956 is written in words as "Nine Hundred Fifty-Six" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: When you can read big math words like 'Nine Hundred Fifty-Six', you are becoming a true math master!

quests.instruction: Which number is smaller: 523 or 445?
quests.question: 523 or 445
quests.hint: Picture counting all the way up -- whichever number you'd reach first is the answer.
quests.explanation: 445 is smaller than 523 -- when counting up, 445 comes earlier!
quests.funFact: If you add 0 to 445, it stays exactly the same: 445!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Count up to 897 in your head, saying each number word as you go.
quests.explanation: The numeral 897 is written in words as "Eight Hundred Ninety-Seven" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: The word 'Eight Hundred Ninety-Seven' helps us communicate numbers without just drawing shapes!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the tens place of 765?
quests.hint: Cover up every digit except the tens digit in 765.
quests.explanation: In 765, the digit 6 sits in the tens place!
quests.funFact: Double 6 is 12! Because 6 + 6 = 12.

quests.instruction: There are 42 groups of ten and 9 more. How many in total?
quests.question: 42 groups of ten and 9 more
quests.hint: 42 groups of ten is the same as counting by tens 42 times.
quests.explanation: 42 groups of ten make 420, plus 9 more makes 429!
quests.funFact: If you count up by ones, 429 comes right after 428!

quests.instruction: Read the word and find the matching number!
quests.question: Four Hundred Fifty-Six
quests.hint: Break the word into parts -- does it sound like a small number, a "teen", or a bigger one?
quests.explanation: "Four Hundred Fifty-Six" is how we say the number 456 in English, so 456 is the digit that matches!
quests.funFact: If you count backwards, 456 comes just before 457!

quests.instruction: Which number is the smallest: 539, 716, or 646?
quests.hint: Compare them two at a time, then keep the smaller one.
quests.explanation: Out of 539, 716, and 646, the number 539 is the smallest!
quests.funFact: Double 539 is 1078! Because 539 + 539 = 1078.

quests.instruction: Read the word and find the matching number!
quests.question: Seven Hundred Fifty-Seven
quests.hint: Say the word out loud, then look for the matching numeral among the choices.
quests.explanation: "Seven Hundred Fifty-Seven" is how we say the number 757 in English, so 757 is the digit that matches!
quests.funFact: If you add 1 to 757, you get 758!

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 896, 625, or 539?
quests.hint: The greatest number is the one you'd reach last while counting up from zero.
quests.explanation: Out of 896, 625, and 539, the number 896 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: If you had 896 apples and found one more, you would have 897 apples!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the ones place of 882?
quests.hint: Cover up every digit except the ones digit in 882.
quests.explanation: In 882, the digit 2 sits in the ones place!
quests.funFact: The number 2 is a single-digit number, meaning it only takes up one spot!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 25, 35, 45, __?
quests.hint: Look at how much bigger each number is than the one before it -- that jump stays the same every time.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 10, so after 45 comes 45 + 10 = 55!
quests.funFact: If you count up by ones, 55 comes right after 54!

quests.instruction: Read the word and find the matching number!
quests.question: Eight Hundred Fifty-One
quests.hint: Say the word out loud, then look for the matching numeral among the choices.
quests.explanation: "Eight Hundred Fifty-One" is how we say the number 851 in English, so 851 is the digit that matches!
quests.funFact: The number 851 is an odd number!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Look at how many digits 731 has, then think of how that word usually sounds.
quests.explanation: The numeral 731 is written in words as "Seven Hundred Thirty-One" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: Did you know? The math word 'Seven Hundred Thirty-One' is spelled with exactly 21 letters!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the hundreds place of 554?
quests.hint: Split 554 into its place-value parts, then find the hundreds part.
quests.explanation: In 554, the digit 5 sits in the hundreds place!
quests.funFact: Double 5 is 10! Because 5 + 5 = 10.

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 10, 35, 60, __?
quests.hint: Look at how much bigger each number is than the one before it -- that jump stays the same every time.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 25, so after 60 comes 60 + 25 = 85!
quests.funFact: If you add 1 to 85, you get 86!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Read the numeral 486 out loud -- what word do you say?
quests.explanation: The numeral 486 is written in words as "Four Hundred Eighty-Six" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: In math, knowing how to read words like 'Four Hundred Eighty-Six' is just as important as knowing the digits!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 25, 75, 125, __?
quests.hint: Add the same jump size again to the last number in the pattern.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 50, so after 125 comes 125 + 50 = 175!
quests.funFact: Double 175 is 350! Because 175 + 175 = 350.

quests.instruction: There are 86 groups of ten and 6 more. How many in total?
quests.question: 86 groups of ten and 6 more
quests.hint: 86 groups of ten is the same as counting by tens 86 times.
quests.explanation: 86 groups of ten make 860, plus 6 more makes 866!
quests.funFact: If you add 1 to 866, you get 867!

quests.instruction: Which number is the smallest: 736, 489, or 567?
quests.hint: Line all three numbers up in counting order first.
quests.explanation: Out of 736, 489, and 567, the number 489 is the smallest!
quests.funFact: If you had 489 apples and found one more, you would have 490 apples!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 875 or 484?
quests.question: 875 or 484
quests.hint: Line the numbers up on a number line in your head -- further right is bigger.
quests.explanation: 875 is greater than 484 -- when counting up, 875 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 875 by 10, it becomes 8750!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the ones place of 691?
quests.hint: Cover up every digit except the ones digit in 691.
quests.explanation: In 691, the digit 1 sits in the ones place!
quests.funFact: The number 1 is a single-digit number, meaning it only takes up one spot!

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 456, 493, or 685?
quests.hint: Line all three numbers up in counting order first.
quests.explanation: Out of 456, 493, and 685, the number 685 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: The number 685 is an odd number!
